ideas.description: Time lever at near-equal math, the one Muon-cost cut not yet tried. Start from tip E031 (commit 3797e1a). First read the Newton-Schulz iteration count in the code. Then profile about 50 steps at each resolution on synthetic data with torch.profiler, recording the NS bmm share per step; this answers H2.4.3 without a separate run. Then change only the iteration count: 5 -> 3 if the code runs 5, otherwise 3 -> 2. Keep the airbench quintic coefficients (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), the pre-normalization, bf16 and the stacked-bmm grouping. Do not use sharper or Polar-Express coefficients: E036 showed that sharpening hurt by 0.47 pp. Recapture both graphs in build. Report per-seed accuracy and the measured NS ms/step before and after.
ideas.expected: Time -0.05 to -0.12 s, to about 5.31-5.38 s. NS bmm is about 0.95 ms/step over about 210 steps, so one fewer iteration removes a third or more of it. Accuracy -0.2 to +0.2 pp vs the pooled 0.7547. E036 suggests a looser orthogonalization acts as a noise filter, so a small gain is possible. Feasible (>= 0.753) is a new best, and the next step is one more iteration cut. A loss >= 0.3 pp means the small-filter tolerance claim (C0097/C0104) fails here, and the iteration count stays.

ideas.description: Explore whether block 3 binds under Muon, as a direct time lever. Block-3 width also sets the largest NS matrix (704x6336), so narrowing it cuts both conv FLOPs and Muon cost. On tip E031, change only the block-3 width, from 704 to 576 (3 convs per block, head input follows). Keep 8.75 ep and nothing else changed. Re-form the Muon groups for the new shapes and recapture graphs in build. Before running, diff commits b0eba3b / 6d40ead / 12fffd2 to settle E013 vs E021's translate amplitude, and record it. Report per-seed accuracy and the pp lost per second saved.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -0.45 s, to about 5.0-5.15 s (the SGD-era 576->704 cost was +0.53 s at 11 ep, plus a smaller NS matrix). Accuracy -0.1 to -0.45 pp. At >= 0.753 this is a new best outright, and block-3 width is not binding under Muon. A rate under 0.56 pp/s (the epoch-cut rate) makes narrowing the next time lever even if infeasible, paired with a margin builder. A rate above 0.8 pp/s confirms block 3 binds, and 704 stays.

ideas.description: Zero-cost margin builder on the schedule end point. The E035 post-mortem and the I029 note say every run decays linearly to about 7% of peak, not to 0. Under Muon's fixed-norm steps, that leaves the final iterate noisy (H6). On tip E031, first confirm the floor value in the GPU LR table. Then change only the end value to 0 for all groups (Muon and SGD), with the same warmup, decay shape and Lookahead. Only the precomputed table changes.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (+/-0.02 s). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.3 pp, centred about +0.1. A paired gain >= 0.15 pp (seed-paired, per E038) supports H4.5.1 and buys about 0.5 ep (about 0.3 s) for a follow-up epoch cut. A loss >= 0.15 pp means the floor is doing useful late-training work alongside Lookahead, which closes the LR-floor axis. In that case, test a higher floor (15%) only if the EMA-tail idea also fails.

ideas.description: Iterate-averaging margin builder, distinct from E039: E039 changed Lookahead decay, which had a flat optimum, and this adds an EMA tail instead. On tip E031, add a Fable-style EMA of all trainable parameters and BN buffers during the final part of the schedule. The EMA updates every 4 steps with decay 0.7, starting about 8 sync points before the LR decay ends, using _foreach_lerp_ inside the captured graph and driven by a GPU step table. At the end of train, copy the EMA weights into the model used for eval. prepare resets the EMA state. Lookahead and everything else stay as they are.
ideas.expected: Time +0.00 to +0.03 s. Accuracy +0.0 to +0.35 pp, centred about +0.15. A paired gain >= 0.2 pp supports H6.1 (averaging is still under-used at the end) and funds a 0.5-ep cut. A change within +/-0.1 pp means Lookahead already captures the averaging benefit, which closes H6.1.

ideas.description: Close the Muon momentum axis; lr is bracketed at 0.24 by E033 and E040. The averaging lever is first-order under Muon (E035), and higher momentum is another form of averaging at zero per-step cost. On tip E031, change only the Muon momentum, from 0.6 to 0.7 (nesterov kept, lr 0.24, same schedule). SGD groups are unchanged. Only the momentum constant baked into the graph changes. This tests H6.3.1's momentum half in isolation (hiverge uses 0.655).
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Accuracy -0.3 to +0.3 pp, centred about +0.05. A paired gain >= 0.2 pp means the short-horizon optimum is at higher momentum: spend it on epochs, then try 0.75. A loss >= 0.2 pp puts the optimum at or below 0.6 and closes Muon constant tuning (H6.3), leaving 0.5 untested only if E031 margin is needed.

ideas.description: Check the code first, then make one architecture change. Read the E031 block definition. If each block already has the airbench96 residual over the last two convs (x = x + x0 after conv2/conv3), record a no-op and do not run. Otherwise add exactly that residual in all three blocks, with dirac init kept. Muon groups and graphs are unchanged in shape and recaptured in build. Nothing else changes.
ideas.expected: Time +0.00 to +0.05 s (one elementwise add per block, fused by compile). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp. A paired gain >= 0.25 pp supports H1.2.6 and becomes margin for the epoch cut or the block-3 576 narrowing. A loss means dirac init already provides the identity path that a residual would add, which closes the idea.

I added 6 ideas, which brings the queue to 7 with I057 still running. The tip is still E031: 5.43 s at a pooled accuracy of 0.7547, a margin of only +0.17 pp.

Since E033 through E040, five axes are closed:
- Muon learning rate (bracketed at 0.24)
- translate amplitude (2 px is the optimum)
- sharper Newton-Schulz coefficients
- batch 3072
- 75% of steps at 24 px

The Lookahead decay test (E039) was inconclusive, so that is left alone too.

**Direct time cuts (2 ideas)**
- **Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations (H2.5.1, priority 5).** One fewer iteration at the same coefficients, with a profile of the per-step cost done first. E036's lesson is that looser orthogonalization is tolerated or even helps, so I expect about 0.05–0.12 s saved at flat accuracy.
- **Block 3 narrowed from 704 to 576 (H1.2.7, priority 4).** This cuts both conv FLOPs and the largest Newton-Schulz matrix, for about 0.3–0.45 s saved. Whether block 3 still binds under Muon has never been tested. Even if this run misses 0.753, the accuracy lost per second saved tells us whether narrowing beats cutting epochs (about 0.56 pp/s).

**Zero-cost margin builders (3 ideas)**
- **LR schedule ends at 0 instead of 7% of peak (H4.5.1).**
- **An EMA tail added on top of Lookahead (H6.1.2).**
- **Muon momentum raised from 0.6 to 0.7 (H6.3).**

I picked these because averaging is the strongest lever on the Muon line (removing Lookahead cost 0.81 pp in E035), and none of them adds time per step. Whatever margin they buy goes into an epoch cut next.

**Explore (1 idea)**
- **Code check for the airbench96 residual in each block (H1.2.6).** It is a no-op if the code already has it.

Two seed-matched reruns (E031 and E038) differed by only 0.07 pp, so a difference of about 0.2 pp between recipes now counts as meaningful.

**Deliberately not queued:**
- The 40%-at-24 px plus 8.0-epoch combination and block 2 at 192: all six world models predicted both would miss the accuracy target.
- Re-testing batch 3072 with the Lookahead cadence held fixed: even a full recovery stays infeasible.
- Polar-Express coefficients with matched update size: E036 already showed sharpening hurts.
- Translate 1 px only during the 24 px phase: E037 showed 1 px hurts.

Nothing was dropped, because no other idea is still queued.
